asparagus-frozen-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Asparagus, frozen, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen cooked asparagus with no added fat is a ready‑to‑eat vegetable that has been blanched, quickly frozen, and packaged without any oils or sauces, preserving its natural flavor and nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the first spring vegetables to appear after winter.
Rapid blanching before freezing locks in the bright green color and crisp texture.
Frozen asparagus can be stored for up to 12 months without loss of taste or nutrients.
In the US and Canada, frozen asparagus is often used in ready‑made dishes such as pastas, omelets, and salads.
Asparagus is rich in antioxidants, including glutathione, which supports the body’s detoxification processes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 kcal, making asparagus an excellent choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Glutathione, vitamin C, and beta‑carotene help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Nutrient loss with prolonged storage
items.content: While freezing preserves most vitamins, very long storage may reduce levels of some light‑sensitive nutrients.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the asparagus in the microwave or by steaming. It works well added to salads, pastas, omelets, soups, or as a side dish for meat and fish. For extra flavor, briefly sauté with garlic and lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen asparagus in its original package in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.

cheese-cottage-cheese-with-gelatin-desse.title: Cottage Cheese with Gelatin Dessert and Fruit

content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese with gelatin dessert and fruit is a combination of smooth cottage cheese, sweet gelatin, and fresh fruit. The cheese provides a creamy base, the gelatin adds a light texture and sweetness, and the fruit contributes aroma and vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is a traditional ingredient in many Eastern European desserts and snacks.
Gelatin is often made from fruit juices, preserving some of the vitamins.
The pairing is popular in children's meals because of its soft texture and pleasant taste.
Fruits can be fresh or canned depending on the season.
These desserts are frequently served in layered glasses or individual cups.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides high‑quality dairy protein important for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in the cheese supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Fruit adds vitamin C, vitamin A and antioxidants that boost immunity.

items.title: Light energy
items.content: Gelatin made from fruit juice offers quick‑acting carbohydrates without heaviness.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Cottage cheese contains probiotic cultures, while fruit provides dietary fiber beneficial for gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cottage cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to dairy proteins.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Gelatin and fruit syrups can raise sugar levels, so those with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Fruit acidity
items.content: Acidic fruits may increase sensitivity of tooth enamel.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cottage cheese with gelatin and fruit chilled in individual glasses or bowls. You can drizzle honey, sprinkle nuts, or add a pinch of cinnamon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container for no more than 2‑3 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors or changes texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen vanilla yogurt is a chilled dessert made from yogurt that is rapidly frozen while being continuously stirred. It combines the creamy tang of yogurt with the sweet aroma of natural vanilla, typically contains less fat than ice cream, and retains live probiotic cultures.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frozen yogurt was introduced in the United States in the 1970s as a healthier alternative to ice cream.
Vanilla flavor is often derived from real vanilla beans, though many commercial products use synthetic vanillin.
The low‑temperature freezing process helps preserve most of the live probiotic cultures.
In some countries it is served with fruit sauces, granola, or nuts.
Sugar levels are usually lower than in traditional ice cream, but they vary by brand.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Yogurt provides live Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium cultures that support gut health.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Like regular yogurt, frozen yogurt supplies calcium important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with ice cream, it generally contains less saturated fat, making it suitable for lower‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yogurt contains vitamins B2 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of vanilla
items.content: Natural vanilla contains vanillin and other compounds with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Yogurt can trigger allergic reactions in individuals allergic to dairy.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some frozen yogurts contain added sugars; check the label if you watch sugar intake.

items.title: Cold shock
items.content: The rapid freezing can cause a “brain freeze” sensation in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen vanilla yogurt can be enjoyed on its own, topped with fresh berries, nuts, granola, or drizzled with fruit sauce. It is convenient to serve in cups or cones.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, consume within 1–2 days to prevent ice crystal formation. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Turnover is a ready‑to‑eat seafood mix that includes shrimp, mussels, squid and fish, pre‑seasoned and lightly fried in aromatic spices. It is designed for quick home cooking and is popular in Asian and Mediterranean cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnover is often sold in vacuum‑sealed packs that keep the product fresh and flavorful for up to 12 months.
The mix may contain seaweed extracts, which boost iodine content and add an umami note.
In Japan a similar product is called “mizu‑moti” and is used as a filling for sushi rolls.
Shrimps are usually peeled but keep the tail for visual appeal.
The product freezes well; thawing is best done in the refrigerator for 8‑12 hours.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Turnover delivers a complete set of essential amino acids for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The mix contains zinc, selenium, vitamin B12 and vitamin D, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, seafood has less saturated fat, making it more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Iodine and vitamin D aid calcium absorption, helping to strengthen bones.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared mixes often contain added salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage or thawing can allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Seafood can contain trace amounts of heavy metals (mercury, cadmium); moderate consumption is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the mix in the refrigerator, then stir‑fry on high heat for 3‑5 minutes with soy sauce, garlic and ginger. Serve with rice, noodles or fresh vegetables. It can also be added to salads, soups or used as a filling for rolls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen Turnover at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 24 hours and store in the refrigerator at +2…+4 °C. Do not refreeze.
